package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all Volusion-hosted stores compromised in the breach)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to steal payment card details from end customers by exfiltrating sensitive data entered on checkout/payment pages to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This constitutes a classic Magecart-style web skimming attack, directly targeting confidential financial information.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when customer enters payment details on checkout page)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into Volusion-hosted store web pages (typically in <script> tags or external JS references)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the checkout form submission, collects payment card details from input fields, and exfiltrates the data to an attacker-controlled domain via a network request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment card data from checkout forms is a hallmark of web skimming attacks and is never legitimate in third-party scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal e-commerce JavaScript should not access or transmit raw payment card data to external domains. Legitimate payment processing is handled by secure, PCI-compliant APIs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or fraud detection scripts may monitor form events, but never transmit full card data to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Access to payment card input fields
Network requests to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains
Obfuscation or encoding of exfiltrated data

attack_chain.action: Attacker breaches Volusion infrastructure and injects malicious JavaScript into customer store pages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in end-user browsers.

attack_chain.action: Injected JavaScript executes in the context of the checkout/payment page, hooking into form submission events.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment card data entered by customers.

attack_chain.action: Collected payment card data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure via network requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment card data for further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript accessing payment card input fields on checkout pages
Event listeners attached to payment or checkout forms
Outbound network requests (XHR, fetch, image beacons) to domains not associated with the legitimate e-commerce provider
Obfuscated or encoded data being sent from the browser during checkout
file_indicators: Unexpected <script> tags or external JS references in checkout/payment pages
JavaScript code not present in official Volusion codebase
References to suspicious or newly registered domains in script sources
network_indicators: Outbound requests from checkout pages to domains unrelated to Volusion or payment processors
Use of image beacons or GET requests with base64-encoded payloads
Domains known to be associated with Magecart or other skimming groups
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized JavaScript modifications on checkout/payment pages, especially scripts accessing payment input fields and sending data to external domains. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) and content security policies (CSP) to block or alert on suspicious script activity. Regularly scan for new or modified scripts in production environments and monitor network traffic for exfiltration patterns typical of Magecart attacks.
